_meta.indication: Veltassa is indicated for the treatment of hyperkalemia; it should not be used as an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalemia because of its delayed onset of action.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: RLY5016-301 (two-part, single-blind Phase 3; Part A treatment phase and Part B randomized withdrawal phase each serving as one of two pivotal studies)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Two-part, single-blind study conducted under Special Protocol Assessment: Part A was a single-arm, two dose-level, 4-week open-label treatment phase; Part B was a randomized, placebo-controlled, 8-week assessment of withdrawal of Veltassa in Part A responders with baseline potassium >=5.5 mEq/L.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with hyperkalemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD); 243 subjects enrolled at 71 sites in 10 countries.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Part A primary endpoint: change in serum potassium (central laboratory) from Part A baseline to Part A Week 4. Part B primary endpoint: change from Part B baseline serum potassium during the randomized withdrawal phase.
pivotal_trials.n: N=243 enrolled in Part A; 107 subjects randomized into Part B (52 placebo, 55 Veltassa).
pivotal_trials.result: Part A: overall mean change in serum potassium from baseline to Week 4 was -1.01 mEq/L (95% CI -1.07, -0.95; p<0.001 vs zero). Part B: estimated median change was +0.72 mEq/L on placebo vs 0.00 mEq/L on Veltassa; difference 0.72 mEq/L (95% CI 0.46, 0.99; p<0.001).

nct_ctgov.title: A Two-Part, Single-Blind, Phase 3 Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Patiromer for the Treatment of Hyperkalemia (OPAL)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%) were constipation (7.2%), hypomagnesemia (5.3%), diarrhea (4.8%), nausea (2.3%), abdominal discomfort (2.0%) and flatulence (2.0%) in patients treated with Veltassa (N=666). Hypomagnesemia was reported in 5.3% of patients.
target_moa: Veltassa (patiromer) is a non-absorbed cation-exchange polymer with a calcium-sorbitol counterion; it binds potassium in the lumen of the colon (exchanging calcium for potassium), increasing fecal potassium excretion and thereby lowering serum potassium.
modality: Small molecule / non-absorbed polymer (cation-exchange polymer; not systemically absorbed)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: BINDING TO OTHER ORAL MEDICATIONS — Veltassa binds to many orally administered medications, which could decrease their absorption and reduce effectiveness; administer other oral medications at least 6 hours before or 6 hours after Veltassa.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design and efficacy endpoints were acceptable.

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients ages 12 to 17 years for treatment of hyperkalemia

citations.quote: Veltassa is indicated for the treatment of hyperkalemia in adults and pediatric patients ages 12 years and older.

summary.text: Veltassa received a standard (full) approval via NDA 205739 submitted October 21, 2014 with a PDUFA goal date of October 21, 2015; efficacy was based on a single two-part Phase 3 trial (RLY5016-301) conducted under Special Protocol Assessment, with Part A and the Part B randomized withdrawal phase each serving as a pivotal study. The application was not referred to an advisory committee, and deferred pediatric studies were required under PREA.

citations.quote:
Date of Submission	October 21, 2014
PDUFA Goal Date	October 21, 2015

Study RLY5016-301 was a two-part, single-blind, phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of patiromer for the treatment of hyperkalemia. The study was conducted under Special Protocol Assessment.
Your application for Veltassa was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design and efficacy endpoints are acceptable.
